info.title: Tented API
info.description:
The Tented public API: generate, publish, and manage AI-built web pages (tents), and run the email platform — contacts, reusable emails, one-time blasts, and triggered flows.

## Authentication
Authenticate every request with a workspace API key: `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>`. Keys are created in **Workspace Settings → API Keys** and are scoped to a single workspace.

## Asynchronous work
Tent generation, bulk creation, and email AI generation return `202 Accepted` immediately. Poll the corresponding status endpoint (`GET /v1/tents/{tentId}`, `GET /v1/bulk-jobs/{bulkJobId}`, `GET /v1/emails/{emailId}/generations/{generationId}`) — no more than every 10 seconds.

## Pagination
Email listings use cursor pagination (`cursor`/`next_cursor`). Blast, flow, and member listings use page pagination (`page`/`limit` with a `pagination` object in the response).

## Conventions
Request and response fields are snake_case, with two exceptions: analytics query parameters (`tentIdOrAlias`, `daysBack`) and segment rule trees (camelCase keys such as `listId` and `timeWindow`).

get.description:
This endpoint has two modes.

**Lookup by identifier** — pass `email` and/or `phone` to fetch a single contact by its normalized email address or phone number. `items` contains the matching contact (including `custom_fields`) or is empty; `pagination` is omitted. When both identifiers are supplied, an email match wins and the phone is only consulted if no contact has that email. Empty identifier values are ignored.

**Paginated listing** — without `email`/`phone`, returns a page of contacts sorted by `sort`/`order`, optionally narrowed by `search` and `updated_after` (contacts updated strictly after an ISO 8601 timestamp — useful for incremental syncs). Listing items do not include `custom_fields`; fetch a single contact with `GET /v1/contacts/{contactId}` for those. Unrecognized query parameters are rejected in listing mode.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Lookup mode: return the contact whose normalized email matches. Supplying this (non-empty) switches the endpoint to lookup mode and listing parameters are ignored.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: Lookup mode: return the contact whose normalized phone matches. Consulted after `email` when both are given. Supplying this (non-empty) switches the endpoint to lookup mode.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Listing mode: page number, starting at 1.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Listing mode: case-insensitive substring match against display name, email, phone, company, first name, and last name.

parameters.name: updated_after
parameters.description: Listing mode: only return contacts updated strictly after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

200.description: Matching contacts. Lookup mode returns 0 or 1 items (with `custom_fields`) and no `pagination`; listing mode returns a page of contacts (without `custom_fields`) plus `pagination`.

items.description: Contacts. In lookup mode, at most one item, including `custom_fields`. In listing mode, the current page, without `custom_fields`.

post.description:
Create or update up to 100 contacts in one request (note: this endpoint's batch limit is 100 items). Each item is matched against existing contacts by a single key: the normalized `email` when the item has a non-empty email, otherwise the normalized `phone`. A matched contact is updated with the item's remaining fields (`status: updated`); an unmatched item creates a new contact (`status: created`, with `original_source` defaulting to `Public API` and `original_source_detail` to `client_item_id` unless supplied).

Because matching uses only that single key, an item whose email is new but whose phone already belongs to a different contact is **not** treated as an update — the creation collides on the phone and the item is rejected with `error_code: conflict` and the conflicting contact in `existing_contact`. (A create collision on the item's own match key — e.g. from a concurrent insert — is resolved as an update of that contact instead.) Updates that would change an email or phone to collide with another contact are likewise rejected with `conflict`, and updates that would leave a contact with neither a valid email nor phone are rejected with `bad_request`.

Partial success is normal — inspect each item result; successful items include the full `contact` with `custom_fields`. Body-level validation failures (an invalid email or phone format, more than 100 items, unknown fields) reject the entire request with `400` before any item is processed.

post.description:
Create a contact import session. Two modes, selected by `source`:

- **`upload`** — returns a presigned S3 `PUT` URL. Upload the raw CSV bytes to `upload_url` with the returned `upload_headers` before the URL expires (`expires_in_seconds`, 15 minutes). Source files up to 350 MB are supported. Only CSV content types are accepted (`text/csv`, `application/csv`, `application/vnd.ms-excel`, `text/plain`).
- **`rows`** — send rows inline as JSON objects (1–1,000 rows). Keys are column headers; the union of keys across all rows becomes the CSV header row. Values are stringified; `null` becomes an empty string. Inline request bodies are limited to 5 MB — larger bodies are rejected with `413` (this keeps requests below the platform's 6 MB payload ceiling, so treat ~5 MB as the practical limit and use `upload` mode for anything bigger).

After creating a session, call `POST /v1/contacts/imports/{sessionId}/preview` to get proposed column mappings, then `POST /v1/contacts/imports/{sessionId}/execute` to run the import. Sessions expire after 7 days and can each be executed once.

No request body. Safe to call repeatedly — for example, after bulk-creating suggested custom fields via `POST /v1/contact-fields`, preview again to see the new fields mapped.

`blocking_issues` must be resolved before executing: an import needs at least one column mapped to `email` or `phone` so contacts can be identified and deduplicated.

target_field.description: Target field `api_name` (e.g. `email`, `firstName`, or a custom field's `api_name`), `listIds` for list-membership columns, or `null` when the column is unmapped.

target_kind.description: Kind of target: `standard` (built-in contact field), `custom` (custom field), `membership` (the column contains contact list IDs to add the contact to), or `null` when unmapped.

reason.description: Why this mapping was proposed (e.g. exact header match, AI suggestion).

source.description: How the mapping was produced: `deterministic` header matching, `llm` (AI-assisted), or `user` (previously approved).

overwrite_behavior.description: Per-column overwrite behavior when updating an existing contact. Omitted on proposed mappings — set it when executing.

ContactImportMapping.description: A proposed column-to-field mapping from the preview step.

header.description: CSV column header. Must be one of the session's detected headers.

target_field.description: Target field `api_name` (standard or custom) or `listIds` for a membership column. Set to `null` to skip this column.

target_kind.description: Kind of target: `standard`, `custom`, or `membership`. Set to `null` to skip this column.

overwrite_behavior.description: When updating an existing contact: `overwrite` replaces the current value; `skip_if_filled` only writes if the field is currently empty. Defaults to `overwrite`, or to `skip_if_filled` when `overwrite_blank_only` is `true`.

row_number.description: 1-based CSV line number, counting the header row as line 1 (the first data row is 2).

header.description: CSV column header the issue occurred in.

target_field.description: Target field `api_name` the column maps to.

ContactImportFieldIssue.description: A field-level validation issue for one cell of the import.

api_name.description: Stable field identifier used as a mapping `target_field` (e.g. `email`, `firstName`, or a custom field's `api_name`).

type.description: `standard` for built-in contact fields, `custom` for workspace custom fields.

value_type.description: Value type. Standard fields may use `email`/`phone`; custom fields are `string`, `number`, `boolean`, or `date`.

is_editable.description: Whether values can be edited manually in the UI. Custom fields only.

field_definition_id.description: Custom field definition ID. Custom fields only.

management_mode.description: Who owns the field: your workspace or a connected integration. Custom fields only.

provenance_kind.description: How the field was created. Custom fields only.

created_from_import_session_id.description: Import session the field was created from, when `provenance_kind` is `import_csv`. Custom fields only.

ContactImportAvailableField.description: A field available as an import mapping target. Standard entries include only the first four properties; custom entries include the full definition metadata.

header.description: Unmapped CSV column this candidate would capture.

suggested_display_name.description: Suggested human-readable label for the new custom field.

suggested_api_name.description: Suggested `api_name` for the new custom field.

suggested_value_type.description: Value type inferred from the column's sample values.

reason.description: Why this column looks like a new custom field.

kind.description: `archived_existing`: an archived custom field already uses this name — restore it instead of creating a new one. `duplicate_suggestion`: another candidate in this preview resolves to the same name.

existing_field_display_name.description: Display name of the archived field (for `archived_existing`).

conflict_key.description: Shared key that groups duplicate suggestions (for `duplicate_suggestion`).

conflicts.description: Empty when the candidate is ready to create as-is. Multiple conflicts can apply to the same candidate.

ContactImportFieldCreationCandidate.description: A suggested new custom field for an unmapped column. Create accepted candidates via `POST /v1/contact-fields`, then pass their IDs to execute as `created_field_definition_ids`.

headers.description: Column headers detected in the CSV.

proposed_mappings.description: Proposed column-to-field mappings, one per header. Use these as the starting point for the execute call's `mappings`.

unmapped_headers.description: Headers with no proposed target (`target_field: null`).

field_creation_candidates.description: Suggested new custom fields for unmapped columns.

items.description: One row: header → cell value (always strings).

sample_rows.description: A sample of the file's first data rows.

sample_issues.description: Validation issues found in the sample rows under the proposed mappings — a preview of the problems the full import would hit.

blocking_issues.description: Issues that must be resolved before execution — currently only `missing_identity_mapping`: no column maps to `email` or `phone`, so contacts cannot be identified.

ContactImportPreview.description: Preview of an import: detected headers, proposed mappings, available target fields, new-field suggestions, and sample validation issues.

import_run_id.description: ID of the queued import run. Poll `GET /v1/contacts/imports/{importRunId}` with it.

import_session_id.description: The import session the run was created from.

duplicate_strategy.description: The duplicate strategy the run will use.

list_ids.description: Static list IDs every imported contact will be added to.

total_rows.description: Total data rows to process, or `null` if not yet counted (counted during preprocessing for upload-mode imports).

correlation_id.description: Correlation ID of the queued background job (useful when contacting support).

ContactImportRunAccepted.description: Acknowledgement that an import run was queued.

import_session_id.description: The import session the run was created from.

file_name.description: File name associated with the import session.

requested_by_user_id.description: Who started the run. `tented-api` for runs started via this API.

duplicate_strategy.description: How rows matching existing contacts were handled.

overwrite_blank_only.description: Whether imported values only filled empty fields on matched contacts.

list_ids.description: Static list IDs imported contacts were added to.

total_rows.description: Total data rows in the source file, or `null` before preprocessing has counted them.

total_chunks.description: Number of processing chunks the file was split into (rows are processed in chunks of up to 1,000).

processed_rows.description: Data rows processed so far — compare against `total_rows` for progress.

last_processed_row_number.description: Highest row number processed so far.

created_count.description: Rows that created a new contact.

updated_count.description: Rows that updated an existing contact.

skipped_count.description: Rows skipped (e.g. duplicates under `duplicate_strategy: "skip"`, or rows with no usable identity).

error_count.description: Rows that failed with an error.

started_at.description: When processing started, or `null` while queued.

created_field_definition_ids.description: Custom fields created during this import's setup.

ContactImportRun.description: An import run: status, chunked-processing progress, and per-outcome row counts.

row_number.description: 1-based CSV line number, counting the header row as line 1 (the first data row is 2).

reason.description: Why the row was skipped or failed. Omitted for clean successes.

contact_id.description: The contact the row created or updated. Omitted when no contact was written.

field_issues.description: Field-level validation issues for this row. Omitted when there were none.

ContactImportRowResult.description: The outcome of a single imported row.

type.description: `standard` for built-in contact fields (read-only, always active), `custom` for workspace custom fields.

api_name.description: Stable identifier used in API payloads, import mappings, and merge tags (e.g. `email`, `firstName`, or a custom field's snake_case name).

value_type.description: Value type. Standard fields may use `email`/`phone`; custom fields are `string`, `number`, `boolean`, or `date`.

is_editable.description: Whether values can be edited manually in the UI. Always `false` for standard fields.

status.description: Field status. Standard fields are always `active`.

field_definition_id.description: Custom field definition ID — the path parameter for `PATCH /v1/contact-fields/{fieldDefinitionId}`. Custom fields only.

description.description: Optional description of what the field stores. Custom fields only.

management_mode.description: Who owns the field: `org_managed` (created in the UI or via this API — fully editable) or `integration_managed` (owned by a connected integration — name, description, and status are locked). Custom fields only.

provenance_kind.description: How the field was created. Custom fields only.

provenance_provider.description: Integration provider that created the field, when applicable. Custom fields only.

provenance_reference.description: Provider-side reference for the field, when applicable. Custom fields only.

created_by_user_id.description: Who created the field. `tented-api` for fields created via this API. Custom fields only.

created_from_import_session_id.description: Import session the field was created from, when `provenance_kind` is `import_csv`. Custom fields only.

show_in_people_list_default.description: Whether the field appears as a column in the People list by default. Custom fields only.

ContactFieldDefinition.description: A contact field definition. Standard fields include only the six required properties; custom fields include the full definition metadata.

api_name.description: Stable identifier: must start with a lowercase letter and contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores. Standard field names (e.g. `email`, `first_name`) are reserved. Cannot be changed after creation.

value_type.description: Value type for the field. Cannot be changed after creation.

is_editable.description: Whether values can be edited manually in the UI.

description.description: Optional description of what the field stores.

show_in_people_list_default.description: Whether the field appears as a column in the People list by default.

error_code.description: `field_definition_collision`: an `api_name` duplicates another item in the request or an existing custom field. `field_definition_cap_exceeded`: the request would exceed the 200-active-custom-field cap.

kind.description: `duplicate_in_request`: two items in the same request use this name. `active_custom`: an active custom field already uses it. `archived_custom`: an archived custom field uses it — restore that field instead.

existing_field_definition_id.description: ID of the existing field, when the collision is with an existing field.

existing_display_name.description: Display name of the existing field, when the collision is with an existing field.

conflicts.description: Present on `field_definition_collision` errors: one entry per colliding `api_name`.

limit.description: The active-custom-field cap (200). Present on `field_definition_cap_exceeded` errors.

current_active_count.description: Active custom fields the workspace already has. Present on `field_definition_cap_exceeded` errors.

attempted_count.description: Fields this request tried to create. Present on `field_definition_cap_exceeded` errors.

source.description: Rule condition source: `contact` for standard fields, `custom_field` for custom fields.

field.description: Standard field name to use as the rule condition's `field` (e.g. `email`, `company`, `tentedScore`). Present when `source` is `contact`.

operators.description: Operator IDs valid for this field (e.g. `equals`, `contains`, `greater_than`, `is_empty`).

field_definition_id.description: Custom field ID — use this as the rule condition's `fieldDefinitionId`. Present when `source` is `custom_field`.

value_type.description: Value type, which determines the applicable operators.

fields.description: Filterable fields: the standard contact fields followed by your active custom fields, sorted by display name.

operators.description: Catalog of all rule operators with display labels.

ContactFieldRuleMetadata.description: Metadata for building audience rule trees.

name.description: List name. Unique within the workspace.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier derived from the name.

kind.description: static = membership managed manually via the member endpoints; dynamic = membership computed continuously from rules; system = auto-managed by the platform (read-only). Immutable after creation.

rules.description: Segment rule tree for dynamic lists; `null` for static lists.

member_count.description: Stored member count for static lists; `null` for dynamic lists — use `GET /v1/contact-lists/{listId}/member-count` for a live count.

owner_campaign_id.description: Set when the list is a blast's inline audience; `null` for user-created lists.

original_source.description: How the contact was first created.

member_added_at.description: When the contact was added to this static list; `null` for dynamic-list members.

source_type.description: How the template was created: `upload` for API- or hand-created templates, `email` for templates saved from an existing email.

source_email_id.description: Email the template was saved from, when `source_type` is `email`.

default_subject.description: Default subject line copied onto emails seeded from this template.

default_preview_text.description: Default preheader text for seeded emails.

default_from_name.description: Default sender display name for seeded emails.

default_from_address.description: Default sender address for seeded emails. Sending requires a verified domain.

default_reply_to_email.description: Default reply-to address for seeded emails.

plain_text_overridden.description: Whether plain text has been manually overridden.

plain_text_overridden_at.description: When the plain-text override was set.

plain_text_stale_after_html_iteration.description: True when HTML changed after a plain-text override, so the override may be stale.

created_by_name.description: Who created the template (API key name or user).

latest_generation_status.description: Status of the most recent AI generation, when one exists.

content_path.description: API path to fetch the latest HTML, e.g. `/v1/email-templates/{templateId}/content`.

plain_text_path.description: API path to fetch the plain-text rendition.

content_path.description: API path to this generation’s HTML (present when `completed`).

plain_text_path.description: API path to this generation’s plain text (present when `completed`).

overridden.description: Whether the text is a manual override.

stale_after_html_iteration.description: True when the HTML has changed since the override was written.

message_id.description: Chat message recorded for the prompt.
